name: Cholera & mosquito-borne
summary: WHO counts over 3,000 cholera deaths in 2026, nearly nine in ten in Africa; outbreaks persist in Sudan, Yemen, DR Congo
state: WHO said on 10 Nov that more than 3,000 people have died of cholera worldwide in 2026, nearly nine in ten in Africa, though deaths in the first nine months were lower than in 2025; Sudan, South Sudan, Yemen and DR Congo were among the most affected countries last year (The Standard, 10 Nov). WHO reported a cholera surge in Yemen as conflict intensified (Al Jazeera, 13 Oct). High mortality in conflict-affected countries keeps the Alert.
for_you: Risk to UK residents is very low. Travellers to affected areas can check NHS and FCDO travel health advice on safe food and water and on cholera vaccination.
rubric_hit: Alert: large outbreaks with high mortality in conflict zones (3,000+ cholera deaths in 2026, WHO 10 Nov; Yemen surge)

sources.title: The Standard — Cholera killed more than 3,000 this year: WHO
Al Jazeera — Cholera cases surge in Yemen as conflict intensifies, WHO says

why: Climate-sensitive diseases — cholera, dengue, chikungunya, Oropouche, West Nile and yellow fever — are hitting record levels and reaching new regions.
drivers: Conflict, floods, heat, El Niño, water and sanitation, mosquito range expansion.

rubric.alert: Large outbreaks with high mortality in conflict zones, or a WHO grade 3 emergency.
rubric.watch: Record-level seasons, or local transmission in countries where the disease was not established (including Europe).
